decision_scope: Do not use native prometheusQueryRange QueryResultCache for any workload that requires read-after-write freshness without an explicit tolerated staleness bound; not an engine bug
source_evidence: src/Interpreters/Cache/QueryResultCache.h: comment explicitly states that the query result cache is not transactionally consistent and is not invalidated by table INSERT or DELETE
src/Interpreters/Cache/QueryResultCache.cpp: Key::operator== compares ast_hash and is_subquery; IsStale compares expires_at with clock; no table data version in key
src/Interpreters/executeQuery.cpp: uses QueryResultCache reader on initial SELECT before query interpreter execution with use_query_cache=1
math_bound: Before second INSERT, 5-minute average of [1] is 1. After appending a sample 3, exact fresh average [1,3] is 2. With fixed AST and TTL=120s, cache must return 1 until cleared/expired if it does not invalidate on INSERT. Verify physical point count 1 then 2 and QueryCacheHits delta to distinguish cache behavior from slow ingestion.
method: Identical native prometheusQueryRange SELECT and settings before/after INSERT (same query SHA); use_query_cache=1 with bounded in-memory backend, TTL=120s, query_cache_min_query_runs=0; control use_query_cache=0; assert physical sample points then SYSTEM DROP QUERY CACHE and repeat. Same runner, source, server and user. No latency/CPU performance claim.
limitations: This is documented expected ClickHouse QueryResultCache behavior, not an unknown source bug.
One single-series native query, fixed timestamps, one INSERT, one cache backend, one TTL and one stock O1 binary; no cross-user, ACL or concurrency cases.
Result cache is explicitly enabled for this test; no claim that Grafana or production has it enabled.
Performance gains or total cost of caching are not measured.

next_action.step: Do not spend new CI on proving the same stale cache behavior. For Grafana dashboards needing freshness use uncached native queries; if bounded staleness is allowed, model TTL vs churn and run a small scheduled query simulation using explicit cache bypass and user/session isolation, without conflating cache speedup with storage-engine optimization.
next_action.stop_condition: Any use of QueryResultCache in the optimization stack must state the accepted max staleness, security isolation and correction behavior; otherwise reject.
